Latin word

putō

putō, putāre, putāvī, putātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

think, reckon; value (with a genitive of value); think, suppose

In this lexicon

  • consider

    also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 11: magnī putāre honōrēs (Lewis & Short)

  • think

    the recommended word · classical · Catull. 12.4: hoc salsum esse putās?; Cic. Fam. 9.3.1: quod velle tē putō; Traupman 393

  • Ego nōn putō.: I don’t think so

    classical

Examples

  • hoc salsum esse putās? fugit tē, inepte

    You think that’s funny? You’ve got it wrong, silly.Catull. 12.4

    In the entry for think

  • quid ergō potissimum scrībam? quod velle tē putō, citō mē ad tē esse ventūrum

    So what shall I write above all? What I think you want: that I’ll be with you soon.Cic. Fam. 9.3.1
